events.content:
Diagnosis is clear. `ProductPage` awaits `getInventory()` at the top level, and `getInventory()` calls `connection()` — a request-time dynamic API. With `cacheComponents: true`, Next.js prerenders a static shell only up to the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary. There is no boundary here, so the whole page — including the static `<h1>` — is deferred until the inventory data resolves.

Fix: move the dynamic read below a Suspense boundary so the title is part of the prerendered shell.

events.content:
Fixed in `app/product/page.tsx:1`.

**Cause:** `ProductPage` awaited `getInventory()` at the top level, and `getInventory()` calls `connection()` (`lib/data.ts:4`) — a request-time API. With `cacheComponents: true`, Next.js prerenders a static shell only as far as the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary. With the dynamic read above any boundary, there was no shell at all, so the static `<h1>` couldn't paint until inventory resolved.

**Fix:** extracted the inventory read into a child component behind `<Suspense>`. The title stays in the parent, so it prerenders; the inventory streams in after.

**Verified:**
- Original code doesn't build — Next.js errors with `Route "/product": Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering`, naming `connection()` outside `<Suspense>` as "blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience."
- With the fix, build passes and `/product` is `◐ (Partial Prerender)` rather than dynamic.
- The emitted shell `.next/server/app/product.html` contains `Premium Widget` and the fallback, but not `in stock` — the title ships in the initial HTML, the data arrives streamed.

Two things worth flagging, both outside what I changed:

- The build was already broken on `master`, not just slow. If you were seeing this as a runtime slowness in `next dev`, the production build was failing separately.
- `getInventory()` returns `Math.random()` values, so it can't be cached with `"use cache"` — streaming was the right lever here. If the real implementation reads a database, caching that call would be faster still, but `connection()` would need to be dropped for that to take effect.

I picked a `Loading inventory…` text fallback to keep the change minimal; swap it for a skeleton matching your design if you have one. Note that Suspense fallbacks reserve no layout space here, so the price/stock lines will shift content as they arrive.
